label: Jiali yak

about.text: The Jiali yak is one of the milked yak populations of China, named in a study of Chinese yak milk. In that study its milk had about 6.8 percent fat, 5.0 percent protein and 16.3 percent milk solids.

sources.text: Opened with WebFetch. Table 1, 'Composition of substances in different types of yak milk (%)', gives Jiali (China): milk solids 16.3, fat 6.8, protein 5.0, lactose 3.6, ash 0.95. The table cites refs 7, 16 and 17 for the whole table; the paper gives no sample size or year for this population. The Tibet location is not in this paper; see origin.

Found in WebSearch text only (page not opened): the DAGRIS country breed pages describe Jiali yak in Tibet. A WebSearch summary of a 2020 Y-chromosome study also places the Jiali-named population in Jiali county. No formation date was found.
Table 1 of the paper, read through WebFetch: fat 6.8, protein 5.0, lactose 3.6, milk solids 16.3 (all %). Single figures, so min equals max.
The paper reports the milk composition of this population, so it is treated as a milked dairy population. No other use was researched.

gaps: Not found: a population count for this breed (the only counts found were for all Tibetan yak), any formation date, the herdbook or DAD-IS entry, the yield per lactation, the risk status, and sample size or year for the composition figures. The paper's Table 1 cites refs 7, 16 and 17 for all rows, not for this row alone. Aka names, domestication and facts were not researched.
